thread:
jessica: FYI customer ACME escalated — their CI started failing after upgrading to redwood-go-sdk v3. Error from `go get`:

```
> go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.0.0
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.0.0: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood/inference-go/@v/v3.0.0.info: 404 Not Found
go: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood/inference-go
	but was required as: github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3
```

They attached their go.mod and CI snippet. They didn't intentionally import /v3, just changed dependency version to @v3.0.0.

sam: Can you paste the customer's go.mod and any `replace` lines? Also which Go version are they using?

jessica: Go 1.20. Their go.mod (redacted):

```
module acme/service

require (
    github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0
)

replace github.com/redwood/inference-go => github.com/acme/inference-go v0.0.0-20260201-abcdef123456
```

They said the replace was added earlier to point at their fork with a small local change.

kevin: This is a classic major-version module path mismatch + replace complication. For Go modules a v3+ major must use an import path that ends with /v3 in the module path. If our upstream module's go.mod wasn't updated to `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3` then `require github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0` is wrong — the correct usage is `require github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3 v3.0.0` and imports must import the /v3 path.

ellen: Also note: because they have a `replace` pointing at their fork (github.com/acme/inference-go) which likely doesn't have the /v3 module path either, the go tool resolves to the pseudo-version from the fork. If the fork doesn't include a proper v3 module path + tag, you'll get the mismatch error.

sam: Repro steps I used locally:
```
mkdir repro && cd repro
cat > go.mod <<EOF
module repro

require github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0
EOF

GO111MODULE=on go get ./...  # fails with same error
```

kevin: Workarounds for the customer:
- Short term: remove the `require github.com/redwood/inference-go v3.0.0` and instead point to the fork with an explicit `replace`/pseudo-version that matches the fork's commits (what they already have) OR vendor the dependency.
- Better short term: change `require` to `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3 v3.0.0` and update imports to use `/v3` paths. (This is intrusive for the customer.)
- Quick unblock for CI: have us cut a compatibility tag on our upstream repo where the go.mod still declares the non-/v3 path but tagged as v3.0.0 — NOTE: that is not semver-correct and can break others; strongly discouraged.

jessica: Customer says they cannot update imports immediately (huge codebase). They just want CI working for the moment.

kevin: Okay we should not make a compatibility tag hack. We'll do the correct fix: patch upstream go.mod to use `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3`, update import docs, and cut/push v3.0.0 tag. That will be the canonical fix. For the immediate unblock I can coordinate with the customer to point their `replace` to our branch that has the fix (so their replace will resolve to a repo that already has /v3 in module path). That avoids changing their imports temporarily if we also adjust the module path? Wait: if their imports don't include /v3, pointing to a repo whose module path includes /v3 will still require them to update imports. So the only non-invasive short-term option is vendor or keep using the forked pseudo-version.

ellen: To be explicit about next actions: I'll open PR that updates module path to include /v3 and bump go.mod, run tests, and then we tag v3.0.0. ETA ~2 hours if no blockers.

sam: I'll reply to the customer with the temporary options: vendor dependency, keep using their fork (we can help produce a fork tag that matches their expectation), or plan for an upstream v3 release in ~2-3 hours.

jessica: Customer prefers an upstream tag — they'd rather be on official release. They're willing to wait a few hours.

ci-bot: Release pipeline queued for branch "release/v3-module-path". CI: 5 jobs queued.

kevin: I'll own the release. After PR merges I'll push annotated tag v3.0.0 and ping you all. Also leaving a note: check for lightweight vs annotated tags — go proxy will only pick up tags normally, but annotated tags are preferred for release tooling.

sam: cool. jessica, can you confirm customer will hold off on local work and wait for us?

jessica: Confirmed. I'll tell them ~2 hours and share this thread. :thumbsup:

kevin: Final note — document this in the repo's release checklist so future major bumps include module path change, update README examples to import /vN, and remind maintainers to push annotated tags.

ellen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference-go/pull/512 — running tests now.
